faqs.question: When is Dussehra in 2026?
faqs.answer: North India celebrates Dussehra on Tuesday 20 October 2026, with Drik Panchang's Vijay Muhurat for New Delhi at 1:59 PM to 2:45 PM. Drik Panchang lists Bengal's Vijayadashami on Wednesday 21 October, and the Mysuru palace calendar also keeps Vijayadashami and the Jumboo Savari on the 21st.

faqs.question: When is Dussehra in 2027?
faqs.answer: Drik Panchang puts Vijayadashami on Saturday 9 October 2027 for New Delhi. Its Bengal Vijayadashami for 2027 is Sunday 10 October, so Bijoya greetings again run a day later than the North.

faqs.question: Are Dussehra and Vijayadashami the same day?
faqs.answer: Yes, they are two names for the tenth day after the nine nights of Navratri, also called Dasara in Karnataka. Bengal calls it Bijoya Dashami, and in 2026 some regional calendars keep it a day later than Delhi does.

faqs.question: When do you say Shubho Bijoya, and to whom?
faqs.answer: Bengali families say Shubho Bijoya after the goddess is immersed on Dashami, not before. Younger people do pranam by touching elders' feet, friends embrace three times (kolakuli), and the greeting carries on through visits in the days that follow.

faqs.question: What do you say when giving apta leaves on Dussehra?
faqs.answer: In Maharashtra the apta leaf is handed over as sona, or gold, and the customary words are 'sona ghya, sonyasarkha raha': take gold, and stay like gold. Juniors usually give it to elders first and bow, then friends exchange leaves.

faqs.question: How do I wish a colleague on Ayudha Puja?
faqs.answer: Keep it about the work: 'May the tools you worship today serve you well all year. Happy Ayudha Puja.' In 2026 Ayudha Puja falls on Tuesday 20 October, the day labs, workshops and vehicles are decorated across South India.

faqs.question: Can I send the same Dussehra wish to everyone?
faqs.answer: You can, but in 2026 a single broadcast on 20 October reaches Bengali and Mysuru contacts a day before their Vijayadashami. A short second message on 21 October, with Shubho Bijoya or Dasarada shubhashayagalu, lands better than the generic line.

faqs.question: What time should I send a Dussehra wish?
faqs.answer: Send it in the morning of the day itself, before the evening Ravan Dahan or the immersion. Our nearest measured analogue is Raksha Bandhan 2026, where 49.4% of SubhSandesh pages were built on the festival day and 27.0% the day before (n = 89), so most people decide late.

faqs.question: Is the Be My Dandiya Partner invitation good for Dussehra?
faqs.answer: Only partly. Navratri's last garba night in 2026 is Monday 19 October, the night before Dussehra, so it suits asking one person for the Sharad Purnima garba on 25 October or next year's Navratri. It is free to use, in English, and one-to-one, so it is wrong for family or office greetings.

faqs.question: Why does Kullu Dussehra start when everyone else's ends?
faqs.answer: The Kullu district administration says Kullu Dussehra begins on Vijayadashami itself and lasts a week. So a Kullu friend is just starting their festival when North India is finishing, and a wish for 'seven good days' fits better than a one-day greeting.

# Dussehra Wishes, Region by Region: Ravan Dahan to Shubho Bijoya

Dussehra wishes land best when they match the Dussehra the other person keeps. In 2026, North India burns Ravan on **Tuesday 20 October**, while [Drik Panchang lists Bengal's Vijayadashami on Wednesday 21 October](https://www.drikpanchang.com/festivals/vijayadashami/vijayadashami-date-time.html?year=2026&geoname-id=1261481) and the Mysuru palace calendar holds its Jumboo Savari on the 21st too. Timing matters more than polish: on SubhSandesh, 49.4% of Raksha Bandhan 2026 pages were built on the festival day itself and 27.0% the day before (n = 89, a different festival, used here as the nearest measured analogue). And 48.3% of shared pages are opened on a phone, so a wish that fits one WhatsApp screen is the safe default.

Below: what each region actually says, original wishes in Hindi, Marathi, Bengali, Kannada and Telugu with romanised text and an English gloss, the 2026 and 2027 dates, and an honest note on when a personalised page is the wrong tool.

## What is Dussehra, and why are there so many greetings for it?

Dussehra, also called Vijayadashami or Dasara, is the tenth day of the bright half of the month of Ashwin, the day after the nine nights of Navratri. Drik Panchang gives two victories for it: Rama killing Ravana, and Durga killing the buffalo demon Mahishasura.

Which victory a family celebrates decides the greeting. A Delhi household says "Happy Dussehra" after the effigy burns; a Kolkata household says "Shubho Bijoya" after the goddess is immersed; a Pune household hands over a leaf and calls it gold. One generic "victory of good over evil" line covers all of them, and fits none of them well.

## Dussehra wishes, tradition by tradition

### 1. Ravan Dahan in North India

**Who:** Most of Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab and Haryana, where Ramlila ends with a Ravan effigy burned at dusk. **2026 date:** Tuesday 20 October; Drik Panchang's Vijay Muhurat for New Delhi is 1:59 PM to 2:45 PM. **What people say:** "Happy Dussehra" or "Vijayadashami ki hardik shubhkamnayein".

- Hindi: पुतला तो हर साल जलता है, इस बार घमंड भी जले। शुभ विजयादशमी!
  *Putla to har saal jalta hai, is baar ghamand bhi jale. Shubh Vijayadashami!*
  "The effigy burns every year; this time may the pride burn too."
- English: "May whatever has been sitting in your head like a ten-headed problem go up in smoke tonight. Happy Dussehra."

### 2. Shubho Bijoya in Bengal

**Who:** Bengali families everywhere, for whom Dashami is the last day of Durga Puja. **2026 date:** Drik Panchang lists Durga Visarjan on Tuesday 20 October and "Bengal Vijayadashami" on Wednesday 21 October, so expect Bijoya greetings across both days.

**What people say:** In food writer [Kalyan Karmakar's account of Bijoya in Kolkata (2021)](https://finelychopped.net/dhaaki-on-the-roof-reinterpreting-durga-puja-traditions-in-the-time-of-covid/), "Shubho Bijoya" is said only after the immersion. Juniors do pranam by touching elders' feet, peers embrace three times and then fold their palms (*kolakuli*), and visits continue for days with tea, snacks and sweets.

- Bengali, to an elder: মা কৈলাসে ফিরলেন, আশীর্বাদটুকু রেখে গেলেন। প্রণাম নেবেন, শুভ বিজয়া।
  *Ma Koilashe phirlen, ashirbadtuku rekhe gelen. Pronam neben, Shubho Bijoya.*
  "Ma has gone back to Kailash and left her blessing behind. Please accept my pranam. Shubho Bijoya."
- Bengali, to a friend: শুভ বিজয়া! কোলাকুলিটা পাওনা রইল, দেখা হলেই।
  *Shubho Bijoya! Kolakulita paona roilo, dekha holei.*
  "Shubho Bijoya! I owe you the hug, first time we meet."

Send the elder's line as a call where you can. A text is fine for peers, but in Karmakar's telling the pranam is the custom, and a forwarded image is not a pranam.

### 3. Apta leaves as "sona" in Maharashtra

**Who:** Marathi families in Maharashtra and Goa. **2026 date:** Dussehra, Tuesday 20 October.

**What people do:** *The Goan* (2019) describes men crossing the village boundary (*simollanghan*) and bringing home leaves of the Apta tree, which are [offered as gold to the women who perform the aarti and exchanged among young and old](https://www.thegoan.net/dussehra-offering-a-slice-of-culture/54656.html). The same report notes the tree is also called *Sona*, and that its heart-shaped leaves are exchanged as gold.

- Marathi: हे आपट्याचं पान सोनं म्हणून घ्या; वर्षभर तुमचं घर सोन्यासारखं उजळू दे. दसऱ्याच्या हार्दिक शुभेच्छा!
  *He aaptyacha paan sona mhanun ghya; varshbhar tumcha ghar sonyasarkha ujalu de. Dasaryachya hardik shubhechha!*
  "Take this apta leaf as gold; may your home shine like gold all year. Warm Dussehra wishes!"
- English, for a Marathi friend abroad: "No apta tree in Toronto, so here is the leaf in words. Consider yourself gifted gold."

### 4. Mysuru Dasara in Karnataka

**Who:** Karnataka's *Nada Habba* (state festival), which the official site dates to 1610. **2026 date:** The [Mysuru Dasara 2026 palace calendar](https://mysoredasara.gov.in/) runs the festival from 11 to 21 October, with Vijayadashami on Wednesday 21 October: Goddess Chamundeshwari receives *pushparchane* in the golden howdah between 4:10 PM and 4:35 PM, and the Jumboo Savari procession leaves the palace for Bannimantap after that.

- Kannada: ನಾಡಹಬ್ಬ ದಸರಾದ ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು! ಚಾಮುಂಡೇಶ್ವರಿ ತಾಯಿ ನಿಮ್ಮ ಮನೆಗೆ ನೆಮ್ಮದಿ ತರಲಿ.
  *Naadahabba Dasarada shubhashayagalu! Chamundeshwari taayi nimma manege nemmadi tarali.*
  "Greetings on Dasara, our state festival! May Mother Chamundeshwari bring peace to your home."
- English: "Watching the Jumboo Savari on a phone screen still counts. Happy Dasara from far away."

### 5. Ayudha Puja and Vidyarambham in the South

**Who:** Workshops, offices, shops and vehicle owners across South India, and children starting school. **2026 date:** Ayudha Puja falls on Tuesday 20 October in both Drik Panchang and the Mysuru palace calendar, which lists it under Mahanavami.

**What people do:** A [study of Ayudha Puja at the Indian Institute of Science (Thomas and Geraci, *Zygon*, 2018)](https://www.zygonjournal.org/article/id/14453/) found scientists decorating labs and vehicles, priests leading the puja, workshops kept shut for two days after it, and faculty handing sweets to neighbouring labs. On Vijayadashami morning, Kerala families also hold Vidyarambham, a child's first writing of letters.

- Telugu: మీరు దసరా నాడు మొదలుపెట్టే ప్రతి పని విజయవంతం కావాలి. విజయదశమి శుభాకాంక్షలు!
  *Meeru Dasara naadu modalupette prathi pani vijayavantam kaavaali. Vijayadashami shubhakankshalu!*
  "May every task you begin on Dasara succeed. Vijayadashami greetings!"
- Kannada, for a colleague: ಆಯುಧ ಪೂಜೆಯ ದಿನ ನಿಮ್ಮ ಕೆಲಸಕ್ಕೆ ಹೊಸ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಸಿಗಲಿ.
  *Ayudha poojeya dina nimma kelasakke hosa shakti sigali.*
  "On Ayudha Puja, may your work find new strength."

### 6. Kullu Dussehra in Himachal Pradesh

**Who:** The Kullu valley, where the festival works on a different clock. **2026 date:** The [Kullu district administration](https://hpkullu.nic.in/culture-heritage/) says Kullu Dussehra begins on Vijayadashami and lasts a week, with traditional songs, dances and dress, so it starts when the rest of North India is finishing.

- Hindi: जब सबका दशहरा खत्म होता है, कुल्लू का शुरू होता है। सात दिन की रौनक मुबारक!
  *Jab sabka Dussehra khatam hota hai, Kullu ka shuru hota hai. Saat din ki raunak mubarak!*
  "When everyone else's Dussehra ends, Kullu's begins. Enjoy the seven days of colour!"

## Dussehra 2026 and 2027 dates at a glance

These are the dates each tradition keeps, checked against Drik Panchang (New Delhi and Kolkata) and the Mysuru palace calendar.

| Tradition | Region | 2026 | 2027 | Greeting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ravan Dahan | North India | Tue 20 Oct | Sat 9 Oct | Happy Dussehra |
| Bijoya Dashami | Bengal | Tue 20 Oct (visarjan), Wed 21 Oct | Sun 10 Oct | Shubho Bijoya |
| Jumboo Savari | Mysuru, Karnataka | Wed 21 Oct | check the palace calendar | Dasarada shubhashayagalu |
| Ayudha Puja | South India | Tue 20 Oct | check local panchang | Ayudha Puja greetings |
| Kullu Dussehra | Himachal Pradesh | starts on Vijayadashami, runs a week | same rule | Hindi greetings |

The takeaway: if you are sending one broadcast message on 20 October 2026, your Bengali and Mysuru contacts are a day early. A second, tradition-specific line on the 21st lands better.

## Happy Dussehra wishes for family, colleagues and friends

Most people send three kinds of message: one to elders, one to work, one to friends. Here are original lines for each, kept under 30 words so they fit a phone screen.

- **Parents and elders:** "Every Dussehra I count the battles you fought for us that nobody saw. Happy Vijayadashami. Touching your feet from here."
- **Colleagues:** "Wishing you a Dussehra that ends one long-pending task for good. See you after the holiday."
- **A friend who just finished nine nights of garba:** "Your feet have earned this rest day. Happy Dussehra, and well danced."

## Is a dandiya invitation right for Dussehra?

Honestly, only partly. Sharad Navratri 2026 runs from 11 to 19 October, so the last garba night is the evening of Monday 19 October, the night before Dussehra.

The one case where it fits: you have one person in mind for next year's Navratri, or for the Sharad Purnima garba on the night of Sunday 25 October 2026. For that, the [Be My Dandiya Partner invitation](https://subhsandesh.in/dandiya-partner) lets you write nine short lines, one for each night, add up to six photos, and send a private link.

Their No button gives up and turns into a second Yes after five tries, and a yes ends in a 1080×1920 Dandiya Pass sized for an Instagram Story. It is free to use (its page schema marks it `isAccessibleForFree`), the page itself is in English, and it is a one-to-one invitation: wrong for a family, society or office greeting.

If what you really want is a plan with that person after the festival, not a garba night, [The Invitation](https://subhsandesh.in/date-invitation) fits better: they answer it, and a yes turns into a countdown to the day. For everything else, [browse all SubhSandesh templates](https://subhsandesh.in/templates).

## When a WhatsApp line beats a personalised page

For Dussehra, most of the time. Occasion-dated pages, every festival and wedding type together, are only 3.7% of what people build on SubhSandesh; 96.3% are romantic and everyday pages.

A page is worth it for exactly one person. A WhatsApp line is better for your building group, your office and your relatives, and a phone call is better for an elder who expects a Bijoya pranam. If you do make a page, 38.5% of creators add a password before sharing, which makes sense for anything personal.
